analysis.title: 'Tis the Season
key_insights: Over the past 30 years, November and December have been among the strongest months for U.S. equities. The S&P 500 has gained 3.7% on average across the two months combined.
The Russell Midcap Growth Index has averaged more than 4.6% across November and December combined over the same 30-year stretch.
Alger suggests the seasonal strength partly reflects investors turning to the following year's earnings, which tends to favor companies with stronger fundamentals.

Consensus estimates call for Russell Midcap Growth earnings to rise 23% in 2027 versus 16% for the S&P 500. Drivers cited are AI infrastructure providers, software with demand rising on AI adoption, and life sciences.
Mid cap growth stocks have trailed larger peers for much of 2026. Alger argues the earnings growth gap may begin to be recognized as attention turns to next year.

Alger says this November's midterm elections may support equities more broadly. It states that resolution of political uncertainty has historically given equities a steadier backdrop in the following year, regardless of the outcome.
Alger's view is that seasonal tailwinds, reduced political uncertainty and the earnings growth outlook align for mid cap growth while the group remains overlooked.

sector_views.rationale: Seasonal tailwinds, reduced political uncertainty after the midterms, and 23% consensus 2027 EPS growth versus 16% for the S&P 500 while the group remains overlooked.

earnings_insights: Consensus estimates (FactSet, as of 10/15/26) for calendar year 2027 EPS growth: Russell Midcap Growth +23% versus S&P 500 +16%. These are estimates, not reported figures.
risk_factors: Past performance is not indicative of future results, and seasonality is a historical pattern, not a guarantee.
Consensus 2027 earnings growth estimates are subject to change, and there is no guarantee the projected growth will be realized.
Growth stocks may be more volatile, and mid cap companies may have limited product lines, financial resources or liquidity.
AI-related companies face competition, rapid obsolescence and other business risks.
